ideas.title: Give your AI agent a memory file it rereads every session
ideas.summary: Persistent markdown memory beats stateless chat for long-running agent work.
ideas.key_ideas:
* A single MEMORY.md index keeps context cheap
* Write-back rules matter more than recall rules
ideas.why_it_matters:
* Stateless agents repeat mistakes they already made
* Memory is the difference between a tool and a teammate
ideas.recommendations:
1. Add a memory index to the agent workspace
2. Log decisions, not transcripts
ideas.transcript: Every session my agent starts by reading one file. That file is its memory. It writes back what it learned before it stops. Sounds boring, but this one habit removed half my repeated corrections.

ideas.title: Ship the boring version first then automate the annoying part
ideas.summary: Manual-first workflows reveal which step actually deserves automation.
ideas.key_ideas:
* Automate the step you dread, not the step that is easy
* A checklist is a valid v1
ideas.why_it_matters: * Premature automation locks in a bad process
ideas.recommendations:
1. Run the workflow by hand five times
2. Automate the single worst step
ideas.transcript: I keep seeing people automate step one of a ten step process. Do it by hand first. The step you start avoiding is the one worth automating. Everything else can stay a checklist.

ideas.title: Voice notes are the highest bandwidth capture tool you own
ideas.summary: Talking beats typing for capturing ideas before they evaporate.
ideas.key_ideas:
* Capture friction kills more ideas than bad ideas do
* Transcription plus tagging makes voice searchable
ideas.why_it_matters: * An idea you never wrote down has zero value
ideas.recommendations:
1. Set up a one-tap voice capture route
2. Auto-transcribe into a reviewable inbox
ideas.transcript: You lose the idea in the time it takes to open a notes app and pick a folder. Voice is instant. Let the machine transcribe and file it. Review once a day, keep or kill.

ideas.title: Stop asking AI for answers start asking it for drafts
ideas.summary: Draft-first prompting keeps the human as editor instead of consumer.
ideas.key_ideas:
* Editing a draft is faster than validating an answer
* Drafts expose the model's assumptions
ideas.why_it_matters: * Answer-mode hides reasoning, draft-mode shows it
ideas.recommendations:
1. Reframe prompts as draft requests
2. Keep final judgment human
ideas.transcript: When you ask for an answer you get confidence. When you ask for a draft you get something you can push against. I only ask for drafts now. My edit is the quality gate.

ideas.title: Small creators win with systems not with volume
ideas.summary: A repeatable pipeline outperforms bursts of motivation posting.
ideas.key_ideas: * Consistency is a systems problem, not a willpower problem
ideas.why_it_matters: * Algorithms reward cadence more than occasional bangers
ideas.recommendations:
1. Define one weekly content loop
2. Measure the loop, not the post
ideas.transcript: The creators who last are not the most talented. They are the ones with a Tuesday system. Build the loop, let the loop make the content, review the loop monthly.

ideas.title: Turn saved videos into a triage queue not a graveyard
ideas.summary: Saved content needs a review loop with statuses or it becomes a landfill.
ideas.key_ideas: * Every capture needs a next action: review, task, or dismiss
ideas.why_it_matters: * Ten thousand bookmarks and zero actions is the default outcome
ideas.recommendations:
1. Add statuses to captures
2. Review weekly, promote the best to tasks
ideas.transcript: Your saved folder is where ideas go to die. Mine used to be too. Now every save lands in a queue with a status. Once a week I promote the good ones into actual tasks and dismiss the rest.

ideas.title: Use a policy engine not vibes to decide what AI can do alone
ideas.summary: Deterministic rules should gate agent autonomy, not model judgment.
ideas.key_ideas:
* Approval tiers beat ad-hoc permission asks
* The model proposes, the policy disposes
ideas.why_it_matters: * Vibes-based autonomy fails exactly when it matters
ideas.recommendations:
1. Write the forbidden list first
2. Log every autonomous action for review
ideas.transcript: My agent can draft anything but it can send almost nothing. That is not the model being careful. That is a policy file being careful. Big difference. Models have moods, policies do not.

ideas.title: The best dashboard is the one that closes the loop
ideas.summary: A dashboard that only displays data is a report; one with actions is a tool.
ideas.key_ideas:
* Every card should have a next-action button
* Read-only dashboards decay into ignored tabs
ideas.why_it_matters: * Display without action creates review debt
ideas.recommendations:
1. Add one primary action per item
2. Wire actions to the real task system
ideas.transcript: If your dashboard just shows numbers, you built a poster. Put the promote button next to the data. The moment I could turn an idea into a task in one click, I actually started using the thing.

ideas.title: Batch your AI experiments like a scientist not a gambler
ideas.summary: Structured experiment logs beat random prompt tweaking.
ideas.key_ideas:
* One variable per experiment
* Keep a lab notebook for prompts
ideas.recommendations:
1. Log hypothesis, change, and outcome
2. Review the notebook before new experiments
ideas.transcript: I wasted a month changing three things at once and learning nothing. Now every experiment gets a line in a log: what I changed, what happened. Boring? Yes. Repeatable? Also yes.

ideas.title: Sell the outcome not the automation
ideas.summary: Clients buy recovered hours and revenue, not workflow diagrams.
ideas.key_ideas:
* Lead with the metric that moves
* The plumbing is your problem, not the pitch
ideas.recommendations:
1. Quantify one outcome per offer
2. Keep architecture out of the first call
ideas.transcript: Nobody wakes up wanting an automation. They want the Friday afternoon back. Sell the Friday afternoon. Show the wiring only if they ask.

ideas.title: Your unfinished projects are inventory not failures
ideas.summary: Parked projects hold reusable parts if you index them.
ideas.key_ideas:
* Index parked work so parts are findable
* Reuse beats restart
ideas.why_it_matters: * Unindexed work is a write-off, indexed work is an asset
ideas.recommendations:
1. Write a one-page index of parked projects
2. Harvest components before starting anything new
ideas.transcript: I stopped feeling bad about unfinished projects when I started treating them like a parts shelf. Half my new builds start with something I already wrote. The index is what makes that possible.

ideas.title: Weekly review is the minimum viable operating system
ideas.summary: A recurring review beats any productivity tool you can install.
ideas.key_ideas: * The review is where systems get repaired
ideas.why_it_matters: * Tools drift without a maintenance loop
ideas.recommendations:
1. Block thirty minutes weekly
2. Review queues, statuses, and one metric
ideas.transcript: Every system I run degrades during the week. The weekly review is the repair shop. Thirty minutes, same time, non-negotiable. Skip it twice and the whole machine is lying to you.
